text: What is GSE309890 about, and what files can I actually download?

## Abstract
GSE309890 is a gene expression profiling study focused on the bacterial organism Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655. The study investigates the effect of the antidepressant sertraline on the emergence of antibiotic resistance, highlighting metabolic changes and pathways such as the pentose phosphate pathway. The series comprises 6 samples and was conducted using high throughput sequencing. The study's data is available through the NCBI GEO repository, including supplementary files that contain processed expression values. The key downloadable file is a CSV-format file containing FPKM (Fragments Per Kilobase of transcript per Million mapped reads) data for all samples. These resources allow for detailed exploration of the underlying molecular biology of sertraline-associated antibiotic resistance in E. coli.

## I. Introduction
Background: The GSE309890 study addresses the role of sertraline, a commonly prescribed SSRI antidepressant, in influencing antibiotic resistance in E. coli through metabolic rewiring. Understanding the molecular basis and metabolic pathways involved informs strategies to mitigate resistance.

Literature Review: No associated PubMed literature records are linked to the GEO record for GSE309890, suggesting unpublished or not yet indexed findings.

Knowledge Gap: Prior to the dataset, the metabolic mechanisms and pathways (like the pentose phosphate pathway) contributing to SSRI-induced resistance were insufficiently characterized.

Objective & Hypothesis: The objective is to provide expression profiling data of E. coli under sertraline treatment and adaptive evolution to understand metabolic changes and bias in resistance emergence.

## II. Materials and Methods
Study Design: The data was retrieved using the NCBI GEO database, specifically querying for accession GSE309890 and requesting both metadata and files.

Materials: NCBI GEO database queried via a dedicated GEO series retrieval tool.

Procedures: The accession "GSE309890" was used to obtain detailed metadata including the study description, sample list, platform, publication status, and links to downloadable files.

Statistical Analysis: Not applicable here, as this query focused on dataset description and availability.

## III. Results

|-----------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Title                       | Antidepressant sertraline biases resistance emergence via stress-driven rewiring of the pentose phosphate pathway: tktA enables metabolic rollback |
| Organism                    | Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655                                                                     |
| Experiment Type             | Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing                                                           |
| Date Published              | 2026/02/01                                                                                                   |
| Platform                    | GPL24659                                                                                                     |
| Sample Count               | 6                                                                                                             |
| Samples Titles              | Multiple samples including controls and adaptive evolution replicates                                         |
| Supplementary Files         | 1 file: GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz (510 KB)                                                           |
| FTP Directory               | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/                                                   |
| Supplementary Files URL    | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz             |
| PubMed Link                 | No PubMed record linked                                                                                        |

## IV. Discussion
Interpretation: GSE309890 contains transcriptomic data illustrating the metabolic impact of sertraline on antibiotic resistance in E. coli. The study highlights the key gene tktA in metabolic rewiring.

Context: The lack of linked PubMed records suggests original or preliminary dataset publication. The supplementary file provides quantifiable expression data for further analysis.

Limitations: No direct peer-reviewed article is associated; conclusions rely on data examination. Only one type of supplementary file is available (FPKM counts), without raw sequencing data.

Conclusion & Future Directions: This dataset offers valuable insights into antibiotic resistance mechanisms in bacteria under pharmacological stress. Future work could explore differential expression and pathway enrichment analyses using these data.

[2] FTP supplementary files URL: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz

Data provided by the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) repository.
